description: Session fixation — attacker pre-sets a session token, victim authenticates with it, attacker hijacks the session

cookie_fixation.description: Set a known session cookie before authentication. If the server accepts the pre-set token after login, the session is fixable.

probes.description: Capture the pre-auth session cookie. Authenticate. Compare the post-auth session cookie. If the value is the same, session fixation is possible.
Set Cookie header to a fabricated session ID. Authenticate. If the server accepts the fabricated token for the authenticated session, fixation exists.

url_session_token.description: Session token passed in URL parameter (e.g. JSESSIONID, PHPSESSID). Attacker can craft a link with their session ID.

probes.description: Append a JSESSIONID URL parameter. If the server associates this session with subsequent authenticated requests, fixation via URL exists.

meta_tag_injection.description: Session fixation via meta tag or HTTP header injection that sets cookies

probes.description: Inject a meta Set-Cookie tag. If the victim's browser sets the cookie from the meta tag (older browsers), fixation is possible.

cross_subdomain_fixation.description: Fixation via a sibling subdomain — cookie scoped to parent domain can be set from any subdomain

probes.description: Check if the session cookie domain attribute is set to the parent domain (e.g. .example.com). If so, any subdomain XSS or control can fix the session.
